literal_first_contact.statement_1: Anything that exists has deviated from symmetry. [Asym]
literal_first_contact.statement_2: Anything distinguishable exists through boundary interaction, by which unbounded symmetry acquires a reference orientation. [Asym] is the resulting relational distinction, not a loss of symmetry.

executive_claim.statement: Anything distinguishable exists through boundary interaction. Boundary interaction gives unbounded symmetry a reference orientation. [Asym] is the relational distinction produced by that reference orientation. [Asym] is not the destruction, negation, or absence of symmetry; it is a symmetry condition through which unbounded symmetry becomes boundedly distinguishable.
executive_claim.compact_form: (*|*) -> boundary interaction -> reference orientation -> [Asym] -> bounded distinguishable symmetry
executive_claim.central_correction: Deviation from symmetry does not mean departure from symmetry. It means symmetry expressed relative to a boundary-conditioned reference orientation.

primitive_distinction_condition.definition: The primitive condition under which distinction is possible.
primitive_distinction_condition.ontological_guard: Not itself a realized object, spatial boundary, physical state, or domain-specific field.

unbounded_symmetry.definition: Symmetry without a bounded reference orientation sufficient to individuate a distinguishable condition.
guards: not an individually bounded existent at the declared scope

boundary_interaction.definition: Any interaction at scope x through which a relational reference orientation becomes established.
guards: involves at least two mutually conditioning positions or one condition and a reference context

reference_orientation.definition: The orientation established by boundary interaction relative to which a distinction becomes expressible.

asymmetry_condition.definition: The relational distinction resulting when unbounded symmetry is evaluated relative to a boundary-established reference orientation.
asymmetry_condition.negative_definition: not symmetry loss, destruction, nonexistence, disorder, or an ontological opposite of symmetry

bounded_symmetry.definition: The boundedly distinguishable symmetry expression produced when unbounded symmetry is conditioned by [Asym]_x at scope x.

primary_mechanism.stage_1: (*|*) means distinction is possible but not yet boundedly realized.
primary_mechanism.stage_2: B_x(>S<, c) is boundary interaction with a condition, context, or relational position.
primary_mechanism.stage_3: B_x(>S<, c) -> o_x establishes a reference orientation.
primary_mechanism.stage_5: <S>_x := Cl_x[[Asym]_x(>S<)] closes as bounded distinguishable symmetry.
primary_mechanism.existence_candidate: Exists_x(c) -> c = Cl_x[D_rel(>S< | o_x)] for some o_x

symmetry_preservation.one_thing_constraint: >S<, [Asym]_x, and <S>_x are orientations or expressions of one symmetry whole, not three substances.

boundary_semantics.anti_substance_guard: The boundary is not an additional substance.

delta_alpha.guard: Does not redefine or reconcile the textbook delta_alpha signature.

notation_and_RT_guards.whole_expression_guard: RT_x[Asym] must not be reduced to <S>_x while source orientation, boundary interaction, or conditioning remains active.
notation_and_RT_guards.atomicity_claim: No listed aspect independently has the complete RT meaning.
notation_and_RT_guards.QM_GR_guard: Does not reconcile independent versus joint projection signatures; QM != GR and neither is directly equivalent to the other.
notation_and_RT_guards.residue: R_Asym,x carries boundary provenance, orientation, source symmetry orientation, admissibility, excluded alternatives, closure scope, realization domain, and ordinal position.

invariants.formula: B_x is not restricted to geometric surfaces

LEM-ASYM-CAND-002 Asymmetry Construction: B_x -> o_x -> [Asym]_x := D_rel(>S< | o_x)

falsification_conditions: A distinguishable bounded condition exists without boundary or reference orientation.
Boundary interaction presupposes the distinction it should generate.
The bounded result is indistinguishable from an ontological zero-state.
The same boundary and orientation yield incompatible results without admissibility distinction.
Projection erases all source orientation and residue.
The mechanism requires a spatial boundary in a claimed nonspatial case.
prohibited_interpretations: [Asym] is absence or destruction of symmetry.
Boundary means only a physical wall.
Reference orientation requires a conscious observer.
Existence is substance added to symmetry.
This packet replaces an existing textbook definition.
